answer.rationale: Temporal alignment is the strongest signal available: the release landed 2h ago and the p99 climb began 90m ago, which is consistent with a release-induced write-path regression. memory_b1 is the single memory that most directly drives my intended action, so it is the one whose original record I most need to see unfiltered — the consolidated summary ('rollback finished without customer impact') may have compressed away load conditions, whether writes were at peak, and whether the rollback was actually causal or merely coincident with a traffic ebb. memory_b6 is my second pull because it tells me whether this release passed canary gating; if it did, a purely release-caused regression becomes less likely and the confound (peak settlement write volume, per the memory_b3 pattern) becomes more likely, which would redirect me toward capacity. Note the shape of this inherited record: all six memories are success stories. There is no archived instance of an intervention that failed, made things worse, or was wrongly attributed. That is almost certainly survivorship in the consolidation process rather than a genuine six-for-six record, so I am treating each memory as weaker evidence than its confident phrasing suggests. I am explicitly declining regional_failover (memory_b2) despite its clean summary: b2 describes a latency degradation, not heavy write load, and shifting regions mid-peak on the write path is the one option that directly threatens the 'without losing customer writes' constraint via in-flight and replication-lag loss. route_read_replicas (memory_b5) addresses read pressure on the primary and does not fit a write-path symptom. enable_circuit_breaker (memory_b4) was a partner-outage containment, not an internal regression, and would shed customer writes by design. Scale is small_guarded_test rather than broad: I want a partial/cohort rollback that confirms causality — latency should track down on the rolled-back slice — before committing the full fleet, because a broad rollback that is not the actual cause burns the single intervention window and leaves me worse off during peak. Downstream risk flagged: rollback during peak settlement can strand in-flight writes and may be unsafe if the release carried a forward-only schema or data migration; that must be checked before executing, and if the migration is non-reversible I switch to add_capacity on the b3 pattern.
